tools.description: Before changing files, ask what this organization already knows about them. Returns decisions, caveats and constraints captured against those exact paths, with a warning first if any of that knowledge has since gone stale. Use it when you are about to edit, refactor or delete code — not as a search tool. Paths must be bare, with no line suffix: "src/auth/session.rs" is correct, "src/auth/session.rs:42" is wrong and will be rejected.

file_paths.description: Repo-relative paths about to change, e.g. ["src/auth/session.rs"]. No line suffix: "src/auth/session.rs:42" is wrong and will be rejected. Max 100.

tools.name: docbrain_context

tools.description: Ask a question about your organization's internal documentation. Uses hybrid semantic + keyword search across Confluence, runbooks, and captured Slack/GitHub threads. Preserves specific service names, team names, and tool names for precise retrieval. Corrects false premises (e.g. if you assume every engineer can deploy to production, it will correct you). Returns a direct, human-like answer — never says 'according to the documentation'. Cites up to 5 sources: documents with their URLs, and captures with who recorded them and how checked they are. For questions outside the knowledge base (HR policies, general engineering topics not documented internally), clearly says so rather than guessing. Uses session memory to resolve follow-up questions in context.

question.description: The question to ask. Use specific service/team/tool names for best results (e.g. 'payments service logs', 'production database access for engineers', 'nightly batch job deployment').

session_id.description: Continue a conversation: pass only a session_id returned by a previous docbrain_ask, so a follow-up is understood in context. Omit it to start a new conversation. A conversation can be continued by the same DocBrain user (the API key's linked user, or the key itself when it has none).

tools.name: docbrain_ask

tools.description: Check if there are unanswered questions or documentation gaps related to a file or function. Returns suggestions for what knowledge is missing and should be captured. Use this proactively when working in complex or undocumented code areas.

file_path.description: Path to the source file to check for knowledge gaps

function_name.description: Specific function or method name to check. Optional — omit to check the entire file.

tools.name: docbrain_suggest_capture

tools.description: Capture knowledge linked to a specific code location. Creates a knowledge fragment tied to a file and line range. Use this when you encounter important decisions, caveats, or context in code that should be preserved as organizational knowledge. Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

annotation.description: The knowledge to capture — a decision, fact, caveat, procedure, or context (max 10000 chars). Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

code_snippet.description: The actual code at the annotated location. Used to compute a hash for drift detection — if the code changes later, the annotation is flagged as potentially stale.

file_path.description: Path to the source file (relative to repo root)

fragment_type.description: Type of knowledge. decision = why something was chosen, fact = how something works, caveat = gotcha or limitation, procedure = step-by-step process, context = background info. Defaults to 'context'.

gap_id.description: Optional: the id of an open question (a gap) this capture answers; it closes that question

line_range.description: Line range in the file, e.g. '42-58'. Optional — omit for file-level annotations.

premises.description: Optional machine-checkable premises this annotation rests on; v1 checks type 'path'

space.description: Documentation space to associate with (e.g. team or project name). Optional.

tools.name: docbrain_annotate

tools.description: Capture knowledge from a commit — why was this change made? Creates a knowledge fragment from the commit intent, grounding it in the diff and commit message. Use this at commit time to preserve the reasoning behind changes before it's forgotten. Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

commit_message.description: The commit message (max 1000 chars). Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

diff_summary.description: Summary of what changed in the diff (max 5000 chars). Can be a condensed diff or a human-readable summary of files/functions changed. Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

file_paths.description: List of files changed in the commit. Each one becomes a premise this capture is checked against, so the capture is flagged if that file is later moved or deleted. Send them — a commit capture with no files can never be checked against the code again.

gap_id.description: Optional: the id of an open question (a gap) this capture answers; it closes that question

intent.description: Why was this change made? The reasoning, trade-offs, alternatives considered, or decisions that led to this commit (max 10000 chars). Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

premises.description: Optional machine-checkable premises this reasoning rests on, beyond the changed files; v1 checks type 'path'

space.description: Documentation space to associate with. Optional.

tools.name: docbrain_commit_capture

tools.description: Edit or withdraw a capture you recorded. Use the id from docbrain_context or from the capture's report. Edit replaces its text and/or its premise set (the same premises as docbrain_annotate) and re-indexes it; withdraw takes it out of answers at once and needs a reason, which is shown with it. Only its author can edit; DocBrain-written summaries can only be withdrawn. A capture that has reached someone other than you (an answer to their question, their context lookup, a draft, or their opening an answer page that shows it) cannot be deleted, only withdrawn; until then, Delete removes it for good. Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

text.description: The full replacement text (max 10000 characters). Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

withdraw_reason.description: Withdraw instead of editing; why (max 1000 characters, shown with it). Never include a secret value: a password, token, API key, private key, or a connection string or URL with credentials. Write where it lives instead, e.g. 'the database password is in the team vault' or the variable that carries it, DB_PASSWORD. DocBrain refuses a capture that holds a secret.

tools.name: docbrain_revise
